data.name: Prithivi
data.gender_notes: Prithivi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Prithivi is the Sanskrit name of the Hindu goddess of the earth. She is the wife of Vishnu and the mother of the gods. She is also known as Pritha, Pritha Devi, and Aditi. Prithivi is often depicted as a beautiful, voluptuous woman with many arms, holding a plough, a lotus, or a trident. The name Prithivi carries the meaning “Earth, Goddess of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Prithivi usually hope their child will grow to embody earth, goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Prithivi represents the earth element and is a symbol of stability, nurturing, and creation. She is the mother of all beings and is often invoked for her protective and grounding energies.
data.etymology: Prithivi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Earth, Goddess of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Prithivi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Prithivi, as the goddess of the earth, holds immense significance in the Hindu culture. She represents the fertile land, the source of all life, and the sustainer of all beings. The Hindu belief is deeply rooted in the idea of a harmonious relationship between man and nature, and Prithivi personifies this bond. Her image is often invoked during agricultural rituals and other ceremonies related to the earth and prosperity. The name Prithivi is also commonly used as a given name to honor the goddess and her protective qualities.
data.spiritual_significance: Prithivi, as a spiritual symbol, embodies the concept of love, nurture, and sustainability. She is the embodiment of the infinite capacity of the earth to give and support life. In Hinduism, the earth is revered as a mother figure, and Prithivi is the personification of this divine motherhood. Beyond the physical dimension, she represents the idea of divine consciousness that underlies all creation and connects everything that exists. Her energy is a reminder of our interdependence with the natural world and the importance of living in harmony with it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Prithivi signifies the earth element in Hinduism, symbolizing stability, nurturing, and grounding. It is the physical and biological foundation of life, representing the maternal and protective force, rooted in the present moment.
